text: Awesome—what was your name?
It's Mason.
Mason, how's it going?
It's going well, thank you.
Do you have a car in stock, new or used?
It's brand new. It's in transit but we have an identical one in-store.
Perfect. I've driven it. I'm in the Bay Area and want the best price.
I'll text you the link; the price is listed.
What discount do you have?
MSRP is $50,034. We're selling it for $48,429 before tax. Lease, finance, or cash?
Probably finance. Maybe lease.
There's a $500 lease rebate.
Run numbers for both.
Are you only looking for silver?
Ideally silver, bonus if it has premium package.
Premium units are spoken for. Let me price you a gray one.
That's fine.
It has a $2,000 discount, ACC, heated rear seats, black/red interior.
Okay, text it to me and call me back.
Will do.
Want to set an appointment?
Let's look at numbers first.
Could we do $3,000 off?
No—one-price store, pre-discounted. But lease-to-buy can save $3–4K.
So around $44K before tax?
Yes. I did one like that today.
Okay. This one doesn't have premium, right?
Correct. But it has heated seats, wheel, moonroof, liftgate, JBL, etc.
Let me think. I wanted silver.
If you don't like it, tell me your number. We *are* negotiable. I'll talk to my manager.
I'm trying for an OTD number. Someone offered $48 and change. Hoping for $47 and change.
I'll try my best. If fair, we finalize. If not, I'll tell you.
Can you send a buyer's order?
Only after pricing approval.
Okay.
I'll get back to you.
Narrator describes $5K add-ons and dramatic tension.
I have good and bad news.
Good news first.
We can do $48,500. Only for you.
I appreciate it. I'll keep shopping.
We dropped from $52K to $48.5K. If too high, be honest; I can try more.
But the car will not go below $48,500. Manager already dropped $3K.
Tell me how much you want down; I'll try.
I'm hoping for closer to $47K.
Give me permission to take it to the manager.
Do your thing.
Your target is $47K?
Yes.
I'll try. If approved, I'll call back.
Sounds good.
Thank you, sir.
